title: Advanced Polynomial Equations
tagline: Year 3 — Sum and product of roots, factor and remainder theorems, higher-degree equations and root relations

introduction.overview: Year 2 solved quadratics by factorising and by the formula. Year 3 looks at the relations between roots and coefficients (Vieta), the remainder and factor theorems for higher-degree polynomials, and equations whose roots are linked by a condition. The relations let you answer questions about the roots without finding them.
introduction.placementRelevance: Questions such as "if α and β are the roots of …, find α² + β²" and "find k so that x − 1 is a factor" are standard in written aptitude tests.
introduction.realWorldContext: Polynomial models in engineering, signal processing and curve fitting rely on root relations.

learningObjectives: Use sum and product of roots
Find α² + β², α³ + β³ and |α − β|
Form an equation from given roots
Apply the remainder and factor theorems

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: For ax² + bx + c = 0 with roots α and β: α + β = −b/a and αβ = c/a.

coreDefinitions: Sum of roots of a quadratic: −b/a. Product: c/a.
Cubic ax³ + bx² + cx + d: Σα = −b/a, Σαβ = c/a, αβγ = −d/a.
Remainder theorem: the remainder of P(x) divided by (x − a) is P(a).
Factor theorem: (x − a) is a factor of P(x) exactly when P(a) = 0.
Discriminant D = b² − 4ac decides the nature of the roots.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: The coefficients are symmetric combinations of the roots, so any symmetric expression in the roots can be rewritten using only the sum and the product.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: Write the sum S and product P first. Then rewrite the target: α² + β² = S² − 2P, α³ + β³ = S³ − 3SP, (α − β)² = S² − 4P.

mainNarrative: Take x² − 5x + 6 = 0. The sum of roots is 5 and the product is 6 without solving. Then α² + β² = 25 − 12 = 13 and α³ + β³ = 125 − 90 = 35.
To form an equation from roots, use x² − (sum)x + product = 0. Roots 2 and −3 give sum −1 and product −6, so x² + x − 6 = 0.
The remainder theorem says the remainder of P(x) on division by (x − a) is P(a). For P(x) = x³ − 2x + 1 divided by (x − 2), P(2) = 8 − 4 + 1 = 5.
The factor theorem is the special case P(a) = 0. If (x − 1) is a factor of x³ + kx² − 4x + 2 then 1 + k − 4 + 2 = 0, so k = 1.
For a cubic, the three relations are Σα = −b/a, Σαβ = c/a and αβγ = −d/a. For x³ − 6x² + 11x − 6 = 0 the roots sum to 6, pairs sum to 11 and the product is 6, giving roots 1, 2, 3.

deepDiveAspects.title: Nature of roots
deepDiveAspects.content: D > 0 gives two real distinct roots, D = 0 equal roots, D < 0 no real roots.

deepDiveAspects.title: Reciprocal roots
deepDiveAspects.content: If roots are the reciprocals of α and β, the new equation is obtained by replacing x with 1/x.

steps.title: Roots

shortcutMethods.title: S and P

traditionalVsShortcut.shortcutMethod: Write S and P, then express the target as S² − 2P, S³ − 3SP or S² − 4P.

rulesForApplication: Never solve if S and P suffice.

placementTips.eliminationTechnique: Test small integer roots by substitution.
placementTips.questionSelectionAdvice: Write S and P before anything else.
placementTips.recruiterInsight: A symmetric target always reduces to S and P.
